result.clarifying_question: Which documented exception do you mean — the specific policy, contract clause, or change-management provision (e.g., its document name/ID and section) — and which pilot change (system, repository, or change request) should the authorization question be evaluated against?
result.rationale: The request asks whether 'the documented exception' authorizes 'the pilot change,' but no source text identifying either the exception or the change was supplied. Both references are decision-changing ambiguities: without knowing which exception document and which change are in scope, any research mission would have to guess at its own subject matter, risking a fabricated scope or invented authority. A single blocking clarification resolves this without guessing; research itself is not inappropriate, so abstention is not warranted.
